clue.text: Suggest cat for one for fur

parts.note: to suggest something is to tip it, as in tipping a horse
a cat is one example of a household pet

explanation.surface: Someone proposes using a cat to supply fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' marks the cat as an example of a wider class, which is the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a fur scarf or cape worn around the shoulders.

clue.text: Bore outsiders in the converse of work

explanation.surface: Something that bores bystanders turns out to be the opposite of getting on with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' looks like 'opposite', but here it is the verb 'chat': to chat about one's work is to talk shop, and that also bores anyone outside the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking shop means discussing your job, which tends to tire listeners outside your line of work.

clue.text: Team goes through road sign getting closer

indicators.note: the team passes through the sign, so it sits inside it

parts.note: STOP is the familiar octagonal road sign
a crew is a team, as of rowers or workers

explanation.surface: A team drives past a road sign as it approaches its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as 'nearer' but is a thing that closes, such as a lid on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is a lid that seals a jar or bottle, so it serves as a closer.

clue.text: Surplus pronoun used by academic

parts.note: PROF is short for professor, an academic
IT is a pronoun

explanation.surface: An academic uses one pronoun too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' just places the pronoun beside the academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the money left over after costs, a surplus of income.

clue.text: Not weighed down with the wherewithal for a picnic?

definitions.text: Not weighed down with the wherewithal for a picnic?

parts.words: Not weighed down with the wherewithal for a picnic?
parts.note: not carrying a hamper, the basket that holds a picnic, and so free of any burden

explanation.surface: Someone sets off light, having left the picnic basket behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhampered means free of hindrance; the joke splits it as lacking a picnic hamper.

clue.text: Run into Weber or another economist

indicators.note: the run goes into the forename of Weber

parts.note: Max Weber was the German sociologist and economist
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A link is drawn from Max Weber to a rival economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weber' stands for his first name, Max, rather than being fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx was a nineteenth-century economist and philosopher, the author of Das Kapital.

clue.text: Returned flashy wedding rings laden with pearls

indicators.note: Returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
rings means the two words encircle the letters wanted, which run across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A showy wedding ring with pearls is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'rings' into the definition, leaving the hidden word with no signal; 'rings' encircles YWED in 'flashY WEDding', and 'Returned' reverses it. The pearls are dewdrops.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy grass is covered in droplets that poets liken to pearls, so it is laden with them.

clue.text: The energy to walk out

explanation.surface: Someone finds the energy to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go means drive or vigour, while literally to get up and go is to leave.

clue.text: Being from the same background, bishop breaks deadlock

indicators.note: the bishop breaks into the deadlock, sitting inside it

parts.note: a stalemate is a deadlock, from chess
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: In a chess game, a bishop's move breaks a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature or person, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse, or person, from the same stable or organisation as another.

clue.text: Here are ice crystals, not diamonds in treasure store

indicators.note: not diamonds tells us to drop that letter from the store

parts.note: a hoard is a stored cache of treasure
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A treasure cache turns out to contain nothing but ice, not diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar is frost, the white feathery crystals of ice formed on cold surfaces.

clue.text: Excluding women from short leg

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at short leg keeps women out of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short leg' is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman, but here 'short' trims a synonym of 'leg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or event is one for men only, so it excludes women.

clue.text: Titania for one is too fond of her scenes?

definitions.text: Titania for one is too fond of her scenes?

parts.words: Titania for one is too fond of her scenes?
parts.note: Titania is a queen in a play, A Midsummer Night's Dream, and a person too fond of scenes is a theatrical overreactor

explanation.surface: An actress playing the fairy queen is accused of hogging the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama queen makes scenes; Titania is literally a queen within a drama.

clue.text: A bit of a shower, Brezhnev, for one

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader is caught in a passing shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leonid is a meteor of the November Leonid shower; Leonid Brezhnev led the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Unearth large work — it could be Bach

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or reshape the letters before it

explanation.surface: A dig uncovers a large work, perhaps by Bach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun for a composition, but it reshapes UNEARTH plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: J. S. Bach was a devout member of the Protestant church founded by Martin Luther.

clue.text: Stones put finally into container that's correct

indicators.note: into places that letter inside the container

parts.note: a case is a container

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of put

parts.note: yes is the reply meaning that's correct

explanation.surface: Someone confirms the stones have at last been placed in their box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts T, the last letter of 'put', inside CASE to make CATSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's eyes are gemstones, such as chrysoberyl, showing a band of light like a cat's pupil.

clue.text: March included a rapid section, which returns

indicators.note: which returns says the section is read backwards
a section of the words included a rapid holds the answer

explanation.surface: A piece of music marked March has a fast passage that repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' takes EDARAP from 'includED A RAPid'; 'which returns' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a formal procession, and to parade is to march in one.

clue.text: A particular bid to absorb business, shortly working together

indicators.note: the bid takes in the shortened business

parts.note: one no-trump, written 1NT, is a bridge bid, here read as INT

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last letter off the word

parts.note: a concern is a business

explanation.surface: A bid aims to take over a company, and the two firms end up cooperating.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge 1NT (one no-trump) is a bid; the figure 1 is read as the letter I. 'shortly' trims CONCERN to CONCER.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act together, jointly and by agreement.

clue.text: Write a line: different line included for everybody

indicators.note: included puts the letter inside the word for write

parts.note: to pen is to write
L is the abbreviation for line, a different one from the railway
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A writer is told to add one line, then slip in another.
explanation.walkthrough: Two abbreviations for 'line' appear: RY, railway, and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenary session is one attended by all members, so it is for everybody.

clue.text: Show disapproval of three-quarter length skirt

indicators.note: keeping three quarters of a four-letter word drops its final letter

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet skirt

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at a calf-length skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarter length' sounds like a hemline but means keep three of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a clicking noise of disapproval.

clue.text: Browser, one recording broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means said out over the air, so the word is heard

parts.note: a taper is one who records on tape

explanation.surface: A web browser records a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests software, but it is an animal that browses on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a forest mammal that feeds by browsing on leaves and shoots.

clue.text: Unusually re-applied to the Order of the Peacock

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rule has been oddly applied again to a knightly order named after a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a chivalric order, but it is the biological order to which the peacock butterfly belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepidoptera is the insect order of butterflies and moths, including the peacock butterfly.

clue.text: Frozen article child makes from tin — have parent tucking in

parts.note: SN is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: the parent is tucked inside the word for have

parts.note: to own is to have
MA is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A child makes a toy from a tin with a parent helping.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowman is a figure of packed snow that children build in winter.

clue.text: Failure must be executed — entering, I shoot

indicators.note: the letter I enters the shortened word
executed means beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: A failure faces execution, and a gunman steps forward to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' is a noun, a young willow stem. Beheading LOSER gives OSER, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow, or one of its pliant young shoots used in basketry.

clue.text: During journey, recruit turned and went obstinately

indicators.note: during puts these pieces within the journey word

parts.note: to ply is to journey back and forth regularly

indicators.note: turned means the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, a recruit
headed means went, as in headed home

explanation.surface: A new recruit turns round mid-march and walks off stubbornly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journey' as PLY means travel a route regularly, as ferries do; the soldier is a GI, an American serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigheadedly means stubbornly, in a way that refuses to give ground.

clue.text: A couple of Scotsmen: pygmies

explanation.surface: Two Scots meet some very small people.
explanation.definitionFit: Twa is Scots for two; the Twa are a pygmy people of central Africa.

clue.text: Final destination a serious distance

parts.note: grave means serious
a yard is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: Reaching one's final destination is a long and serious journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is where everyone ends up, the last resting place.

clue.text: Through song, English recreated past events

parts.note: by means through or via

indicators.note: recreated says the letters are created again in a new order

explanation.surface: Old times come back to life through an English song.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygones are things of the past, as in let bygones be bygones.

clue.text: Disdain to be hard on influential director

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an auteur is a film director whose personal style shapes the film

explanation.surface: Being tough on a celebrated film-maker shows contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' sets H above AUTEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughty pride, a lofty disdain for others.

clue.text: Character finds time to go through two articles

indicators.note: time passes between the two articles, inside them

parts.note: THE is the definite article
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A character in a story finds time to read two articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter, here of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Where van Gogh worked, as his self-portrait endlessly shows?

indicators.note: endlessly removes the first and last letters

parts.note: Van Gogh painted himself with a bandaged ear after cutting it off, so he appears without an ear

explanation.surface: Van Gogh's self-portrait reveals where he painted.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-portrait with bandaged ear, painted after he cut off part of his ear, shows him lacking it; trimming the ends gives the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is the Provence town where van Gogh lived and painted in 1888 and 1889.

clue.text: Sort of dance exploit

explanation.surface: A kind of dance used to take advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap is dancing with metal-tipped shoes; to tap a resource is to exploit it.
